data.narrative:
Rangeview is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Cameron Schiller and Aeden Gasser-Brennan, having raised $5M+ to date. The relevant peer universe comprises 9 private companies and 1 public entity (277810.KQ) in Robotics & Manufacturing, including comparables such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

Given Rangeview's stage and data constraints, valuation relies on stage-progression analysis. Using the $5M total raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $12M. This method is applicable where peer-median triangulation is not; the sector contains 11 same-sector peers, but insufficient narrow peer clustering (fewer than 3 datapoints meeting same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier criteria) precludes reliable median-based calibration without risking misleading extrapolation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This narrow $3M band reflects reliance on a single methodological pillar. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient close-stage comparables to validate stage-progression assumptions and limited visibility into Rangeview's unit economics, market position, or technology differentiation relative to the identified peer set. A fuller valuation would benefit from additional Series A or late-seed comparable data within the robotics subsector.
